title: Red states, blue states
hook: Americans choose their president in 51 separate contests. Thirteen elections, 1976 to 2024, show the map flipping, hardening and coming down to a handful of states.
notes: Results: MIT Election Data and Science Lab, 'U.S. President 1976–2024' (Harvard Dataverse, doi:10.7910/DVN/42MVDX, version 10, CC0). The map shows who won the most votes in each state and DC, with a candidate's votes on several party lines added together (New York and others allow this). Maine and Nebraska can split their electoral votes by congressional district; the map shows only the statewide winner. Shares are of all votes cast for president in the state; the national shares in the text are sums of the state results. Lighter colours mean a smaller winning share (50% or less is lightest, 70% or more darkest). Electoral-college outcomes and the 537-vote Florida margin of 2000: Wikipedia, '2000 United States presidential election' and '2016 United States presidential election'; the seven swing states of 2024: Wikipedia, '2024 United States presidential election' (read October 2026). State shapes: Natural Earth.

scenes.title: Fifty-one contests
scenes.text: Each state and DC picks its own winner, who almost everywhere takes all of its electoral votes. In 2024 Donald Trump won 31 states and Kamala Harris 19 plus DC. Lighter shades mark closer results; step through the elections since 1976.

scenes.title: Landslides
scenes.text: In 1984 Ronald Reagan won 49 states; Walter Mondale carried only his home state of Minnesota and DC. Reagan had won 44 states four years earlier. Since George H. W. Bush won 40 in 1988, no candidate has carried more than 32.

scenes.title: The South changes sides
scenes.text: In 1976 Jimmy Carter of Georgia won every Southern state except Virginia. In 2024 the Republican won all of them except Virginia. Georgia swung from a 34-point Democratic win to a 2-point Republican one.

media.title: Republican lead over the Democrat, percentage points

scenes.title: More votes, fewer states
scenes.text: Twice the candidate with the most votes nationwide lost the electoral college.

options.text: In 2000 Al Gore won 48.3% of the national vote and George W. Bush 47.8%. Bush won the electoral college after carrying Florida by 537 votes out of almost 6 million.
In 2016 Hillary Clinton won 48.1% of the national vote and Donald Trump 46.0%. Trump won the electoral college, carrying Michigan, Pennsylvania and Wisconsin by less than one point each.

scenes.title: Seven states decide
scenes.text: Most states now vote the same way every time: 35 states and DC have backed the same party in every election since 2000. Campaigns concentrate on the few that swing. In 2024 Trump won all seven swing states; Wisconsin, Michigan and Pennsylvania by less than two points.
